title: Giving notice over no written music; Play the same note
summary: He gave notice wanting to learn to read, and Basie advised him to play the same note every night if it sounds good.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well now, let me see, in '37, now the band -- you say they were mostly head??
Well now, how does that change?

Well, I -- we had rehearsals -- no, didn't have no rehearsals, just go in the band and -- I really got sort of -- got to the point where I wasn't accomplishing what I really wanted to accomplish, you know. Because I knew that I wasn't -- I didn't want to make Basie's band my whole life, you know.

So there was no music in the band and I told him one night -- I put in my notice. I said I'd had it, you know. And he said, 'What is this?' I said, 'I really want to, you know, learn how to read very good. I want to be a very -- I want to be a good musician, you know. And you take Ed Lewis and all those guys that had been in Benny Moten's band, they had been playing the same thing. When you're in on the beginning of a hit arrangement, nobody can play it like you, because you're in on the beginning of this. You've got your note and you contribute some to it, you know.
So I told him, 'Out the Window,' 'John's Idea,' 'Swinging the Blues,' We had a thing called 'Daisy Chain,' all those

Yeah, they all knew it. So he says, "Well, you sound good." I said, "Well, I don't know what note to hit, you know. Every night I'm trying to pick me a note to play all this." He said, "Well, if you find a note tonight that sounds good, play the same damn note every night," you know. So that's -- that was the beginning of a very beautiful friendship.
He said, "If you find a note tonight and it sounds good, play the same damn note tomorrow night. Every night, play the same note."
But, you did -- I mean, gradually you had to have arrangers.
Oh, yes. As time went by, you know, you can't stay in the same -- can't stay in the same area of anything that you did 30 years ago and be successful. You've got to change with the time.
But I mean, in that period, you know, after -- let's see, the tenor players change, let's say.
